stories.source_title: Digital fraud surges to 88%: The hidden security crisis chilling cross-border finance

stories.headline: Digital Fraud Surges Across African Financial Institutions
stories.dek: Cross-border financial expansion faces severe headwinds as institutions report soaring digital fraud rates and low PAPSS integration.
stories.body: Financial institutions across the continent are navigating a tense security landscape as digital fraud climbs dramatically, reaching up to 88 percent in certain sectors. A recent survey spanning 20 African countries reveals that nearly half of all surveyed financial entities are choosing to prioritize domestic growth over international expansion in response to the mounting risks. As cyber threats and fraud attempts grow more sophisticated, institutions are expressing clear caution regarding cross-border operations. Compounding this challenge is the low adoption rate of Africa's primary cross-border payments infrastructure. According to the data, only 11 percent of the surveyed institutions have established connections to the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System, commonly known as PAPSS. This hesitation to integrate into the flagship network underscores the deep-seated security concerns chilling broader regional trade and financial connectivity. For the fintech and banking sectors, balancing the urgent demand for robust security measures against the ambitions of continental expansion remains the defining test of the current economic cycle.

The high-level meeting occurred the day after the major summit wrapped up its proceedings in the Russian capital. While details surrounding timelines and financial frameworks remain forthcoming, the dialogue signals a notable step in energy diplomacy between the two nations. As Ghana continues to evaluate its long-term power generation capacity, nuclear energy has emerged as a key point of international cooperation. The developing partnership will be closely watched by regional energy analysts as discussions between Presidents Putin and Mahama progress further.

stories.source_title: Nigeria’s AI ambitions depend on building for local realities
stories.source_excerpt: Nigeria’s AI progress will be judged by the local problems it solves, panellists said at “The State of AI in Nigeria", a session at Moonshot by TechCabal.
stories.headline: Panelists at Moonshot by TechCabal Emphasize Local Impact for Nigerias Artificial Intelligence Growth
stories.dek: Experts during The State of AI in Nigeria session argued that future success relies entirely on addressing domestic challenges.
stories.body: The trajectory of artificial intelligence development in Nigeria must be anchored in practical, domestic applications to achieve meaningful success. This was the core consensus shared by industry experts during a dedicated session titled “The State of AI in Nigeria,” hosted as part of the Moonshot by TechCabal conference. According to insights highlighted by TechCabal, the true measure of the country's technological advancement will ultimately depend on how effectively homegrown solutions address everyday local hurdles. Industry leaders gathered at the event to debate the future of emerging tech within the nation. They stressed that copying foreign frameworks without tailoring them to the local environment will limit the potential of the ecosystem. Instead, the focus must remain on building tools and infrastructure that resonate with the realities experienced by everyday citizens and businesses across the country. As the conversation around artificial intelligence gathers momentum, stakeholders continue to advocate for strategies that prioritize indigenous problem-solving over generic adoption.

stories.source_title: Ebola deaths top 5,000 as fear of continent-wide spread mounts
stories.source_excerpt: Deaths in Congo’s Ebola outbreak have topped 5,000 as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease and cases are recorded in other African countries, the latest government data on Saturday shows
stories.headline: Congo Ebola Deaths Surpass 5,000 Amid Regional Transmission Anxieties
stories.dek: Fresh governmental numbers indicate that fatalities in the country's ongoing crisis have crossed a grim threshold.
stories.body:
According to official data released on Saturday, the death toll from the Ebola outbreak in Congo has officially surpassed the 5,000 mark. The country continues to battle the persistent and relentless transmission of the virus.

As the health crisis wears on, government figures highlight mounting anxiety regarding a potential continent-wide transmission. These fears are compounded by the confirmation of additional cases popping up in other parts of Africa.

Public health monitors are closely watching the situation as the virus continues its spread.

The latest metrics underscore the profound severity of the ongoing public health challenge faced by authorities in Congo and the wider region.

stories.headline: MTN Nigeria Pulls in N4.61 Trillion Revenue in Strong Nine-Month Financial Showing
stories.dek: The major telecommunications company posted a significant 59.4% jump in pre-tax profit for the period ending September 30, 2026.
stories.body:
MTN Nigeria Communications Plc has reported its financial performance for the nine months concluding on September 30, 2026. The telecommunications giant registered a notable surge in profitability alongside substantial revenue generation.

Data shared by Nairametrics reveals that the company's pre-tax profit advanced by 59.4 percent. This upward trajectory brought the total pre-tax profit figure to N1.80 trillion for the evaluated three-quarter timeframe.

Alongside the profit growth, revenue figures reached an impressive milestone. MTN Nigeria pulled in a total revenue of N4.61 trillion over the course of the nine-month period.

The robust financial update reflects continued commercial activity and operational scale for the telecoms enterprise within the Nigerian market during 2026.

stories.source_title: Intra-African payment rails are key to cutting cross-border friction, says Grey
stories.source_excerpt: Grey is building direct payment connections and currency pairs in African markets so cross-border transfers no longer use the dollar.
stories.headline: Grey Advocates for Direct African Payment Rails to Bypass Dollar Dependence
stories.dek: The fintech platform is actively developing native currency pairs and direct payment links to ease cross-border money movement across the continent.
stories.body:
Financial technology platform Grey has emphasized the critical necessity of establishing internal African payment infrastructure. According to the company, building robust intra-African payment rails is essential for eliminating the friction that currently burdens cross-border financial transactions.

In commentary reported by TechCabal, Grey outlined its strategic approach to bypassing traditional intermediary currencies. Rather than routing regional transfers through the dollar, the organization is engineering direct payment connections.

As part of this initiative, Grey is actively establishing dedicated currency pairs tailored to various African markets.

The push for localized currency routing aims to make transferring funds across different African nations faster, cheaper, and less dependent on foreign reserve currencies.

stories.source_title: Stablecoins gain ground in African trade but face hurdles to wider use
stories.source_excerpt: Stablecoins are giving African businesses an alternative way to pay overseas suppliers, but costs, security concerns and fragmented blockchain networks remain obstacles to wider use, industry executives told Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos.
stories.headline: Stablecoins Emerge as Trade Tool Across Africa Despite Roadblocks
stories.dek: Industry leaders meeting in Lagos indicate that digital currencies offer alternative payment channels for international vendors.
stories.body:
Digital tokens are increasingly becoming a preferred mechanism for enterprises across the continent to settle accounts with international suppliers. According to industry executives speaking at a gathering in Lagos, these tools provide a practical alternative for cross-border financial transactions.

Despite the growing adoption, several barriers continue to impede widespread integration. Stakeholders at the Moonshot event organized by TechCabal highlighted that high expenses, lingering safety worries, and disconnected blockchain infrastructures present significant obstacles.

The discussions underscored both the potential and the limits of digital assets in modern commerce. While businesses look for faster and more reliable ways to manage foreign trade, market participants stress that structural challenges must be resolved before broader implementation can occur across the region.

stories.headline: Former Railway Workers Call on President Tinubu to Resolve Housing Deadlock
stories.dek: Nigerian railway pensioners are pressing for federal intervention regarding stalled housing monetization guidelines.
stories.body:
Former employees of the Nigerian railway sector have launched an appeal directed at President Bola Tinubu. The group is urging the administration to step into an ongoing disagreement concerning the federal government housing policy.

The core of the dispute centers on the failure to execute the housing monetization framework specifically designated for these pensioners. For many elderly workers, the resolution of this issue is critical to securing their post-service welfare.

As the appeal reaches the highest office, affected retirees hope that presidential intervention will break the administrative stalemate. The ongoing disagreement highlights persistent concerns regarding pension administration and the fulfillment of welfare commitments to former public servants.
